notes: Village markets and tradesmen's restaurants may not have card machines; carry cash in TL.
Distances between bays and villages are long and the municipal dolmuş runs infrequently; renting a scooter or car makes the days much easier.
July is very hot between 12:00 and 16:00; stay in the shade or in the sea at those hours and drink plenty of water.
In restaurants, tip 5-10% of the bill; it is generally not added automatically.
At places where a family still lives, such as Can Yücel's House, a photo from the doorstep is enough; do not enter the garden without permission.
Datça's coast lies close to Mediterranean monk seal habitat; take care not to leave litter in the coves.
When visiting village cooperatives such as Sındı, letting them know in advance is a sign of mutual respect.

niche.name: Sındı Village Agricultural Development Cooperative Olive Oil Factory
niche.why_hidden: A village cooperative founded in 1948 that still produces with traditional stone presses. No Datça tour stops here; only the producer families in the area and the cooperative's customers know the facility exists.
niche.access_instructions: From central Datça, take the D400 towards Marmaris to Sındı Mahallesi, about 16-21 km and 25 minutes by car. Ask at the cooperative building in the village square and they will point the way; you need to let them know before visiting.
niche.local_contact: Instagram @sindikoyukooperatifi üzerinden DM, ziyaretten en az 1 gün önce.
niche.season: The shop and tastings are open all year. October to December is the olive harvest and pressing season, the busiest time to see production live.
niche.insider_tip: Bring a small glass jar: they fill it with freshly pressed oil and sell it well below supermarket prices, and it is much fresher.
niche.show_reason: Tarihi üretim yöntemi, kooperatif dayanışması ve samimi tadım deneyimi bir arada; taş bina fotojenik ama sosyal medyada neredeyse hiç görünmüyor.
niche.address: Sındı Mahallesi, Kooperatif Binası, Datça, Muğla

days.theme: The heart of Datça: stone lanes and sunset at the pier

stops.name: Old Datça Stone Streets
stops.tips: Wander aimlessly through narrow stone lanes draped in bougainvillea; the best light falls around 10 in the morning. Stopping to photograph doorways in the shade of almond trees is fine with most homeowners.

stops.name: Craft Street
stops.tips: Buy oya (needle lace), dried flowers and almond cookies from the village women's stalls. Bring cash, as card machines are rarely available. Some stalls close towards noon because of the heat, so it is better to go in the morning.

stops.name: Can Yücel's House
stops.tips: The house is only open to visitors on 12 August. At other times you can photograph the lines of poetry on the door and the gravestone in the garden. It is on Dere Sokak in Reşadiye Mahallesi; keep quiet, as the family still lives inside.

stops.name: Zekeriya Sofrası
stops.tips: Chard soup and chard borani are the classics here. Arrive around 13:00, before the daily home-style dishes run out. At Eski Datça Çarşı Sokak No:1, it serves a filling lunch at tradesmen's-restaurant prices.

stops.name: Kekik Restaurant
stops.tips: Right on Kumluk Beach, with grilled octopus and sea bass with almonds as good choices. Reserve on summer evenings if you want a table with a sea view. Besides fish, try the Aegean-style dishes cooked in olive oil.

stops.name: Sapphire Roof
stops.tips: Have a cocktail on the Sapphire Hotel terrace against the lights of Datça harbour; the half hour just after sunset is the calmest. No reservation is needed, but in summer it helps to arrive a little early to get a table.

backups.name: Eski Meyhane
backups.tips: A small, friendly meyhane (tavern) known for its melon and shrimp meze. Head here if the main stop has no space. It is in central Datça, and you can go without calling ahead.

backups.name: Kargı Bay
backups.tips: It is 3 km from the centre, reached by municipal dolmuş (minibus) or a 30-minute walk, and the beach is completely free. If you buy something to eat or drink, sunbeds and umbrellas are free too.

days.theme: Journey to the western tip: Knidos and hidden coves

stops.name: Mehtap Cafe
stops.tips: A family-run garden house for 20 years, serving an organic spread village breakfast. Ask for a lighter version before boarding the boat. It is in Old Datça, a 10-minute drive from the harbour.

stops.name: Datça Bays & Knidos Day Boat Tour
stops.tips: The route usually stops for swimming in coves that are hard to reach by car, such as Mersincik and Kızılbük, then anchors at the ancient city of Knidos. Lunch is included in the price. Once you step ashore at Knidos you pay an entrance fee of about 200 TL (Museum Pass accepted), so carry cash.

stops.name: Meyhane Datça
stops.tips: A friendly meyhane in the harbour area known for its liver and ribs; the seafood meze are good too. It fills up early on summer evenings, so arriving around 19:00 is key to getting a seat.

stops.name: A Jazz Bar
stops.tips: Live jazz plays on certain evenings of the week, within walking distance of the pier. You can sit and listen even if you do not order a drink. At weekends, go a little early to find a table.

backups.name: Emek Restaurant
backups.tips: Run by a father-and-son fishing family beside Datça harbour, where the sea beans and octopus salad stand out. Fresh fish varies with the day's catch.

backups.name: Ovabükü Beach
backups.tips: A little-known, quiet cove. The car park is small, so you need to go early in the morning. Consider it as an alternative swimming stop if the tour boat does not call there.

stops.name: Palamutbükü Beach
stops.tips: The public beach is free. For sunbeds and umbrellas, you can eat something at nearby businesses and use them at no charge. The water is at its most turquoise in the midday sun.

stops.name: Liman Restaurant
stops.tips: The stone-oven octopus and sea bass with almonds are a must here; it is known as the best restaurant in Palamutbükü. Go early at lunchtime, as the waterfront tables fill quickly.

stops.name: Hayıtbükü Beach
stops.tips: Go on a weekday: weekends are crowded and sunbeds get pricier. The beach is ringed with restaurants and cafes, and even the walk is worth it for the views.

stops.name: Bonito Restaurant & Beach & Bar
stops.tips: A clean, calm spot in Hayıtbükü, with meze and fresh fish on the evening menu. Book early for a table facing the sunset.

backups.name: Palamutbükü Neighbourhood Market
backups.tips: Held one day a week, the market sells fresh olives, cheese and meze ingredients. If the main restaurant has no space, you can pick up snacks and eat them on the beach.

backups.name: Karaincir Beach
backups.tips: A less crowded alternative to Palamutbükü. The shade of the pine trees is welcome in the midday heat.

days.theme: Olive and honey trail: Mesudiye, Sındı and Emecik

stops.name: Mesudiye Village
stops.tips: Explore the village on foot; at the producers' stalls by the roadside you can find fresh almonds and bitter orange. Mesudiye is also known for its lemon and pomegranate orchards.

stops.name: Derin Bahçe
stops.tips: The gözleme (stuffed flatbread) made by local women and the omelette with organic eggs stand out here. You can also buy the olives, honey and jams they produce in the garden. A cool, shady spot to sit at midday.

stops.name: Sındı Village Agricultural Development Cooperative Olive Oil Factory
stops.tips: Tour the historic factory, which produces with stone presses dating from 1948; cooperative members explain the process during a tasting. Let them know on Instagram a day before your visit. If you bring a small glass jar, they will fill it with freshly pressed oil.

stops.name: Aktur Bay
stops.tips: A calm, pine-scented cove belonging to Emecik village. In the village nearby you can also see scattered remains from the Byzantine period. Locals mostly work in beekeeping and olive growing.

stops.name: Elaki Restaurant
stops.tips: In the garden of the 200-year-old Mehmet Ali Pasha Mansion, with most ingredients coming from its own organic gardens. The stone-oven dishes shine in the evenings. It is at Reşadiye Kavak Meydanı.

backups.name: Garavilla Restaurant
backups.tips: Inside Otel Mavi Beyaz, it offers Aegean and Mediterranean dishes prepared with local herbs. A good alternative if the main stop is full.

backups.name: Kızılbük Bay
backups.tips: A quiet cove that is hard to reach by car and usually visited by boat; a good extra stop if you want to stretch the day.

days.theme: Kızlan windmills and sunset at Aktur

stops.name: Kızlan Windmills
stops.tips: On the Datça-Marmaris road, six stone mills lined up from bottom to top. Do not miss the morning light for the best photos. The village's windy position is why the mills were built here.

stops.name: Kızlan Village
stops.tips: Pure honey from high-altitude pine forests is bought here directly from the producer; be sure to taste the pine honey. It is well below supermarket prices, and they can fill your glass jar.

stops.name: Rumeli Köfte ve Ciğer
stops.tips: A family-run tradesmen's restaurant specialising in köfte with piyaz (bean salad) and liver. It is busy at lunchtime, so go a little early. Affordable and filling.

stops.name: Aktur Iskele Beach Club
stops.tips: Known as the spot where the sun sets last in Datça, with sea and music among the pine trees. Buying a drink is enough to use a sunbed.

stops.name: Hestia
stops.tips: With about twelve kinds of mantı (Turkish dumplings), it gives traditional flavours a modern touch; try the Uzbek mantı. It is on Reşadiye Çarşı Sokak, and booking is recommended in the evenings.

backups.name: Iskele Neighbourhood Market
backups.tips: Set up on Balıkçı Sokak, the market sells fresh fish and seasonal vegetables. Go early in the morning to get the freshest produce.

backups.name: Ilıca Water Mill
backups.tips: A historic water mill next to Taşlık Beach and a so-called 'soda lake' said to have healing properties. A good stop if your route changes.

days.theme: A day in the town centre: market, crafts, meyhane

stops.name: Datça Saturday Market
stops.tips: At the market ground at the end of Ambarcı Caddesi you will find fresh olives, local cheese and handmade textiles. Go early in the morning, as the best produce sells out towards noon.

stops.name: Datça Sofrası
stops.tips: The oldest restaurant in Old Datça, with köfte and dishes made with Datça almonds standing out. Meze with Aegean herbs and güveç (clay-pot stews) are popular too.

stops.name: Kumluk Beach
stops.tips: Close to the centre and ideal for a short cooling-off break; a calm, uncrowded beach.

stops.name: Zada Meyhane
stops.tips: There is no fixed menu: they serve whatever the day brings. A small, boutique meyhane at the entrance to Old Datça. Seats are hard to find at weekends, so go early.

stops.name: Coop Live
stops.tips: One of the lively options on the pier, with acoustic concerts and DJ sets. Entry is usually free; you only pay for drinks.

backups.name: Culinarium
backups.tips: German-Turkish-Italian fusion cooking; the almond semifreddo is a must. On Iskele 64. Sokak, with sea views, and booking is advised.

backups.name: Domuz Beach
backups.tips: A small, quiet cove close to the centre, which you can consider as an alternative to Kumluk Beach.

days.theme: Before goodbye: coffee, a quiet cove, souvenirs

stops.name: Nokta Pastanesi
stops.tips: A light morning coffee with almond cookies and poğaça (savoury pastry). Within walking distance of the pier, it is ideal for starting the last day without tiring yourself out.

stops.name: Kurubük Bay
stops.tips: A calm, unspoilt cove with no facilities at all. Bring water and snacks; you will need to leave your car by the roadside and walk a little.

stops.name: Datça Village Products Factory Shop
stops.tips: The shop continues the traditional production dating from 1948; you can buy olive oil, honey and almond products as souvenirs. Vacuum-packed items are sold in sizes that fit in a suitcase.

stops.name: Eski Ev Cafe
stops.tips: A light farewell lunch in Old Datça with gözleme and handmade mantı; do not miss the almond coffee. In its quiet garden, enjoy Datça's peace one last time.

backups.name: Poseidon Fish House
backups.tips: A relaxed lunch with fresh seafood and wine; a good alternative if the main stop has no space.

backups.name: Bağlarözü Bay
backups.tips: Like Kurubük, a calm cove with no facilities; a little-known spot favoured by locals.
